script: Oh I played the long game . I am by no means an expert, or pro, at revenge but I am a patient person. Seven years ago I finally snagged my own place after ten years of grind. I'd saved, hustled, and the joy of owning my own pad was real. Being single and on a mortgage meant compromises, so I picked a shared block—cheaper, freehold, no strata. But when I moved in, the landlord from the unit next door knocked, asking about insurance. I asked for a copy, and it was a strata policy. I was like, "Wait, what? This is a freehold?" The lawyer shook his head, and the title was misrepresented. I got a meeting with the agent, printed out emails that said it was freehold, but he was all "no fault, no offer." I went to mediation and only asked that when I sold, they'd cover the costs. He offered me a thousand bucks to stay away—no thanks. I could have sued, but my health and the cost made me hold back. So I started plotting. I found his Facebook—no privacy, photos of a "Boys on Tour" trip months after I bought. I also pulled his address from a business registry. Every anniversary of the sale, for six straight years, I sent flowers with a note: "Dear Real Estate Agent Remembering you, on this, our special day. She has your eyes. Love Elle." The wording stayed the same, only the flowers changed. Then it hit me: he'd recently divorced, lost his home and his agency. His wife found out he'd cheated, and the "special day" was the anniversary of his affair—just a year before I bought. He's now a wreck: no house, half his savings, business gone. I feel a tiny pang of guilt sometimes, but I remind myself he's a scumbag. Karma's patient, spiteful, and I am a patient, spiteful, vengeful bitch. (But here's the thing, bestie—his life's already a mess, and I just keep it going.) And honestly? I am watching him unravel, and the more he falls, the more I know this… (So wait—what's next? )
